item.title: Chris Brown’s Ex-Housekeeper Wants to Dip Into R&B Tour Profits for $13 Million Dog Attack Verdict
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends. Today, we're talking about a developing story involving Chris Brown and a former housekeeper who's owed a significant amount of money.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: According to a recent court ruling, Chris Brown owes his former housekeeper, Maria Avila, $12.9 million in damages after she was mauled by a 200-pound dog on his property in 2020. However, Avila's attorney claims that Brown has made no effort to pay the judgment, despite being on a lucrative nationwide tour with Usher.
[Short pause]
Host: The tour, which kicked off in June, is expected to generate substantial revenue, and Avila's attorney is seeking to have a portion of those profits earmarked for the unpaid judgment. In fact, Avila wants a judge to freeze Brown's touring accounts to preserve her access to the funds.
[Soft music continues]
Host: The incident that led to the lawsuit occurred in 2020, when Avila was attacked by a Caucasian shepherd named Hades while emptying trash outside Brown's home. The attack resulted in permanent facial disfigurement, scarring, vision loss, and nerve damage.
[Short pause]
Host: Brown had accepted some liability for negligence but disputed the extent of Avila's injuries. The case went to a jury trial, and ultimately, the jurors sided with Avila, awarding her $12.9 million in damages.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's the latest on this story. We'll continue to follow it and provide updates as more information becomes available. Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more news and trends.
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
